summary: Tested the SOC Series AI cover art and the weekly series email on both backend and frontend. Backend: 12/12 pytest tests passed. Covered: AI covers on all 15 written posts (each a unique, valid 200 image/webp); unwritten posts keep the section image; an admin cover link overrides the AI cover; auth on POST /admin/series/{id}/cover; /me/series/next and the series_emails preference toggle; admin email-test returns {sent:1} and writes no send record; unsubscribe with a bad token (400) and a valid HMAC token (200, sets the flag false); cron weekly-digest (401 without auth, 200 ack in under 1s, 9 series_sends for 9 active students all set to post #001, no duplicates on a second run in the same week, a reused run_id is flagged duplicate, next post moves to #002). Frontend: all 125 series cards and the post-page cover load with no broken images, and the 15 AI covers are unique. The student toggle shows ON with the next-email link, switches to OFF, stays OFF after reload and was turned back ON. Admin: 125 row thumbnails load; the test-email toast appears; on post #015 'New AI cover' showed 'Making cover...' and the preview changed to a new version (1280px) after about 15s. Not tested: the optional 'write with AI' then auto-cover flow (skipped to save LLM credits and keep post state; checked by code review only). Cleanup done: series_sends emptied, new digest_sends records and TEST_ cron_runs deleted, no users with series_emails=false, so real Monday sends start at #001. The cron test also sent the weekly threat digest once to seed users (expected).

minor.issue: The post number comes from all_posts() over READY posts only, so it is the post's place among written posts, not its series number. The public list counts all published posts. If a later post (for example #040) is written before #016-#039, the email subject and the 'Your next email' link show #016 while the card shows #040.

The series_sends record is written before send_email, and send_email swallows errors. If the email provider fails, the student never gets that post but it is marked as sent, and the 'sent' count still goes up.

The prompt says 'no text', but some covers contain text (post #005 shows labels 'Security Events / Alerts / Incident / Case'). Also, old cover files are never deleted from object storage when a cover is remade.

ui_bugs.issue: No try/catch around the PATCH call, so a failed call shows no error toast (unhandled promise rejection).

action_items: Use the global series number (from the list of all published posts) in send_series_week and /me/series/next, not the index among ready posts.
Optional: only record series_sends after a successful send_email, or delete the record if the send fails.
Optional: add try/catch with an error toast to SeriesEmailToggle.flip.
Optional: remake cover #005 (it has visible text) and delete old storage objects when a cover is remade.
critical_code_review_comments: Post numbers for emails and 'next' are computed from ready posts only, so they drift from the public numbering once posts are written out of order.
Send records are written before delivery, so a failed send still consumes the post.
Covers are cached in process memory (CACHE, up to 61 entries). This is fine for now, but each worker keeps its own copy.
seed_data_creation: None kept. Remade the AI cover for post #015 'How to Perform an Effective SOC Investigation' (id 39f1e1543789, new v=110ef144). Temporary cron and series_sends data was cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_series_cover_email.py. Its cron test deletes ALL series_sends and any digest_sends created during the run, so do not run it after real Monday sends exist in prod data. The 'write with AI' then auto-cover flow is still untested end-to-end.
